records.reason: m129 at 2/1 establishes the lower-ratio member of a fixed-loading thioether-aldehyde pair. Together with its selected 10/1 point, it tests whether the predicted steep response transfers from the related thioether ketone, whose measured 10/1 behavior is late (2f72c334253bbe94a8ab, 596bd04bfe916866f908).

m129 at 10/1 has predicted V1/V2 of 37.08/63.65 mL despite no measured labels for this molecule. Its 2/1 companion distinguishes a scaffold-wide retention offset from a steep ratio response, making this more informative than an isolated extreme prediction.

m115 at 1/1 supplies a baseline for the selected 10/1 point. The para-methoxy ketone is unlabeled, while the ortho analog has measured condition-dependent behavior (c40d715383d042030e93, 50fbcf5ece9bd5fc2d70). The within-m115 comparison holds loading fixed; cross-isomer comparisons also account for their different loading solvents.

m115 at 10/1 is predicted at 16.14/31.73 mL. Paired with 1/1, it tests the magnitude of the predicted increase and provides a carbonyl/substitution contrast to measured m127, without assuming that the two methoxy positions share a response curve.

Unlabeled aminoacetophenone m36 at 1/1 tests transfer of nitrogen-containing scaffold representations. Related amino ester m86 is measured at 7.13/14.69 mL under its own 1/1 conditions (e9744f740f6e67fa561d), while the tertiary-amino ester m19 recently exposed substantial underprediction (a595d5f1882c39914392).

m36 at 2/1 completes a fixed-loading pair with its 1/1 point. The predicted increase from approximately 4.75/12.71 to 8.70/21.00 mL tests whether aminoaryl ketones need a different response slope from the measured amino ester and aminonitrile families.

Diphenyl sulfoxide m199 in pure EA establishes a baseline in a structurally distant, unlabeled sulfur-oxygen family. Paired with 5/1 at the same loading, it separates a missing scaffold interaction from an incorrect solvent-response slope.

m199 at 5/1 is predicted to finish at only 14.28 mL. Strong silica interaction through S=O is a chemical prior that makes this modest prediction worth testing. The pure-EA companion gives the result an interpretable condition contrast.

Unlabeled aromatic dialdehyde m191 at 2/1 supplies the baseline for its selected 10/1 point. Measured substituted aldehydes span very different responses, including m28 at 10/1 (351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a) and m193 at 10/1 (a01a137fa48c1391b9e7), so aggregate carbonyl count is insufficient evidence for transfer.

m191 at 10/1 is predicted at 16.57/36.58 mL. Its paired 2/1 label will test whether a second aldehyde produces a steep retention response or whether the model is importing broad behavior from other polar aromatic families.

The unlabeled, sterically hindered ketonitrile m47 has low maximum structural similarity to measured molecules. This 5/1 point tests transfer of combined nitrile/carbonyl interactions from aromatic examples such as m31 (156594686f5cf7182bcc), extending coverage where aromaticity and carbonyl accessibility differ.

Unlabeled alpha-bromo ester m77 at 20/1 connects measured bromoester neighborhoods with different alpha substitution. The recent m76 5/1 result was underpredicted at acquisition (f106b85660c480a44538), so this moderate predicted regime checks functional-group transfer beyond the heavily sampled tail families.

m19 in pure EA, at the same 50-uL loading as its recent 1/1 measurement a595d5f1882c39914392, tests whether stronger eluent restores ordinary retention. This anchors the newly discovered amino-ester failure region instead of inferring its entire curve from one label.

m19 at 2/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 10.95/18.25 mL, earlier than the measured 1/1 result of 15.61/25.51 mL (a595d5f1882c39914392). Together with the selected pure-EA point, it directly tests this unverified nonmonotonic model response at fixed loading.

m80 at 5/1 and 100 uL tests the model's interior retention maximum. Measured 2/1 and 50/1 points at this loading are ordinary (0b1b7bf04ed8169cd172, 08155ffdcb0d27576050), whereas this candidate is predicted at 10.56/17.86 mL.

m80 at 20/1 and 100 uL complements the selected 5/1 point and measured 2/1 and 50/1 endpoints. It tests whether the predicted hump declines across intermediate ratios or is an artifact of fitting the ordinary 50/1 labels.

For m45, the supplied SMILES identifies a bromo carboxylic acid. This 10/1, 50-uL point bridges measured 5/1 and 20/1 at the same loading (5cc67d02b8fad1c648d6, b24f66ff77974f8ba6e1). It tests the large increase without extrapolating from the anomalous 50/1 record 129036e0bccc4ff7e848.

m107 at 1/1 fills the solvent-response gap between measured pure-EA, 2/1, and 5/1 behavior (d76d74e2a624a532f9f8, 143bf510fe2028583763, c6924324ddd95f249df6). Its 100-uL loading also broadens local coverage, although comparisons with the 50-uL curve must retain that loading difference.

m66 in pure EA completes the strong-eluent baseline for the same 100-uL loading used in measured 1/1 and 2/1 points (8f5acbec0c511bb1ea89, 4659b6752f23c0b85f08). Both acquisitions underpredicted V2 substantially; this label distinguishes a baseline offset from a rapidly increasing pyridyl-ketone response.

m205 at 2/1 and 150 uL follows measured 1/1 at the same loading (1aceeb0ee0419209d1c7) and precedes the late 5/1 observations at other loadings (7954bf73f74c7fbcecb2, 48853fd78c77153b963a). It locates the transition in this aromatic alcohol family.

m200 at 1/1 and 150 uL bridges its measured pure-EA baseline (88d94bacb5a3b54ac7d1) and the broad 2/1 result (f91285c618eacb53538b). This fixed-loading solvent contrast tests where completion becomes late in a nitro-substituted alcohol.

m200 at 2/1 and 50 uL forms a direct loading contrast to f91285c618eacb53538b at 150 uL. Its predicted 29.04/65.49 mL contrasts with that measured 19.65/68.02 mL, testing whether lower loading mainly delays onset while completion remains similar.

m13 at 5/1 and 100 uL fills a large gap between measured 2/1 and 10/1 regimes (74ce463c8423fbd22dc4, 9e3f598e00375ec93d9b). The predicted 26.11/58.50 mL is an intermediate hypothesis, useful for learning the curvature of a multi-carbonyl, ether-containing scaffold.

m60 at 10/1 and 150 uL completes a three-level loading series. The measured 50- and 100-uL points shift from 46.02/68.74 to 39.13/64.72 mL (beda2205eedbe1688e1f, c352863d9fa4a8645481). The third point tests continuation or saturation of the endpoint-specific loading trend.

m119 at 2/1 and 150 uL directly contrasts with the measured 50-uL point a775926fce57b3bf9ec1. It tests loading dependence near the transition preceding the late 5/1 measurement 776ee2c1e85ebde75168, helping distinguish amount effects from scaffold-level tail transfer.

m89 at 20/1 and 100 uL bridges its measured ordinary 10/1 neighborhood (4b39568fb3ff725fec83) and late 50/1 point at the same 100-uL loading (249b884b29177edb9df5). It tests whether the amino ester's large increase appears gradually or beyond an intermediate ratio.

m128 at 5/1 and 150 uL fills the gap between measured 2/1 behavior (21e09d52eac22fe25e15, at 100 uL) and 10/1 at 150 uL (596bd04bfe916866f908). This labels the thioether-ketone response before comparing it with the new m129 aldehyde curve.

m87 at 10/1 and 50 uL provides a loading contrast to the measured 150-uL result ef809aee1c6b06021475 and a same-loading ratio contrast to 50/1 in 810b16f35a3a86f451ce. These two references help distinguish loading effects from the predicted aromatic-ester response slope.

m174 at 100/1 extends a measured benzyl-benzoate response beyond 30/1 (92bac523bed1042d6a75, 34cf0942ff52b1b80385). It tests weak-eluent extrapolation in an ester family whose measured volumes are moderate, providing a useful counterweight to polar-scaffold tail examples.

m91 at 50/1 and 150 uL extends the measured 10/1 point a93680d827624e459a39 at identical loading. Comparing this unsaturated diester with ordinary 50/1 m80 observations tests whether carbonyl arrangement changes the ratio response despite shared acceptor count and TPSA.

Unlabeled anisole m126 at 50/1 is predicted in the ordinary 5.40/10.77-mL regime. It tests the unsubstituted aromatic-ether neighborhood against measured halogenated ethers and low-retention anchors such as 717cada2bf06f3f3af6a, without presuming novelty requires late elution.

Unlabeled branched arylalkyl chloride m50 at 5/1 has zero hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors and an ordinary 5.02/7.53-mL prediction. Its low structural similarity supplies a distinct calibration test for nonpolar chemistry alongside the condition-sensitive polar experiments.

hypotheses.content: Scaffold identity controls whether PE-rich conditions produce late completion. Diethyl malonate m80 remains ordinary at 50/1 across the measured loadings, while its predicted intermediate-ratio hump and transfer to differently arranged diesters remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The model needs scaffold-by-condition interactions rather than a universal relationship between oxygen count, predicted interval width, and late completion.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m80 have a genuine interior retention maximum at fixed loading, and does the unsaturated diester m91 follow a different weak-eluent response?

hypotheses.content: Loading can shift onset and completion differently. Several matched families show appreciable V1 decreases with increased loading while V2 changes less or increases; the direction and magnitude vary by scaffold and ratio.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched labels can teach density-times-volume effects separately for V1 and V2, addressing the nearly invariant loading predictions seen in many candidate pairs.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m60 loading trend continue at 150 uL, and do m200, m119, and m87 show analogous endpoint-specific loading shifts?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing families need scaffold-specific solvent-response corrections. Recent m66 and m19 measurements weaken transfer from generic ordinary-retention predictions, while m212 demonstrates that loading also changes the apparent response.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A shared nitrogen descriptor can conceal differences among pyridyl ketones, tertiary amino esters, aminoaryl compounds, and secondary amines.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do fixed-loading m19 labels confirm the predicted nonmonotonic curve, and how do m36 and m66 behave across stronger-eluent baselines?

hypotheses.content: The predicted ratio responses of unlabeled m129, m115, and m191 are testable structure-by-condition effects. Paired measurements can distinguish a retention offset from a steep slope without assuming that carbonyl identity, substitution position, or acceptor count guarantees transfer.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These pairs interrogate specific extrapolations into thioether-aldehyde, para-methoxy-ketone, and aromatic-dialdehyde neighborhoods and connect them to measured analogs.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed loading, do the measured changes agree with the predicted 2/1-to-10/1 or 1/1-to-10/1 increases, or are the model's baselines or slopes incorrect?

hypotheses.content: Diphenyl sulfoxide may interact with silica more strongly than its modest predicted 5/1 retention suggests. This is a chemical prior, and the magnitude of the effect in the supplied loading conditions is unknown.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The unlabeled S=O environment is poorly connected to measured structures; a paired solvent contrast can reveal whether the representation misses scaffold affinity or solvent dependence.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are m199 labels elevated at both pure EA and 5/1, or does the discrepancy emerge mainly in the weaker mobile phase?

hypotheses.content: Retention often increases nonlinearly as PE/EA rises and the mobile phase weakens, with scaffold-dependent transition locations. Anomalous and nonmonotonic records prevent imposing a universal monotonic response on every row.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate labels constrain endpoint-specific curvature and reduce reliance on extrapolation between ordinary and very late regimes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do the m45, m107, m205, m200, and m13 curves change most rapidly, and does the moderate m174 response extrapolate to 100/1?

hypotheses.content: Predicted interval width or high retention alone does not identify error. Ordinary-retention chemistry can retain moderate bias, while broad predictions have produced errors of either sign.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Ordinary anchors help preserve calibration across the Row-distribution as high-error condition-response regions receive additional labels.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the unlabeled m77, m126, and m50 neighborhoods follow their ordinary predictions or expose transferable functional-group and structural biases?

feedback_interpretation: The latest m80 midpoint confirms ordinary 50/1 behavior across all three measured loadings, so further sampling of that endpoint has lower value; I instead test the remaining predicted interior hump. At acquisition, m66 2/1 underpredicted V2 by 21.91 mL, m107 2/1 by 12.40 mL, and m19 1/1 by 15.19 mL. These outcomes favor local response measurements and targeted nitrogen-family exploration. Conversely, m94 10/1 overpredicted V2 by 12.99 mL, while several ordinary anchors were close, weakening any global tail-expansion correction. The m60, m128, and m89 loading contrasts reinforce separate learning of onset and completion. I also correct inherited interpretation: larger PE/EA ratios are weaker eluents, and m45 is a bromo carboxylic acid according to its SMILES. Its negative-V2 50/1 record remains anomalous evidence rather than a mechanistic template. Historical acquisition errors guide attention here and are not treated as current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch forms connected experiments around existing labels. Fixed-loading pairs for m19, m80, m36, m115, m129, m191, and m199 distinguish baseline errors from condition-response errors. Intermediate conditions for m45, m107, m205, m200, m13, m89, and m128 locate transitions that endpoint-only sampling leaves ambiguous. Loading contrasts for m60, m200, m119, and m87 test whether V1 and V2 respond differently to amount. The m91 and m174 extensions probe distinct weak-eluent responses, while m47, m77, m126, and m50 cover specific structural gaps and ordinary-retention calibration. Cross-molecule analogies retain differences in recorded loading amount, solvent, and solvent volume; they do not establish isolated structural causality. I avoided selecting duplicate condition tuples within the batch and used CW distance, quantile widths, and novelty as coverage cues rather than calibrated epistemic uncertainty. The expected benefit is better learning of structure-condition interactions across both ordinary and late rows, rather than optimizing the chromatography of the chosen experiments.
